payload.text:
The amber light finds Greyhollow Ford gone quiet in the wrong way — no bell, no ferry-keeper's call across the water, only the river shouldering past its banks and not one bird in the reeds. The ferry sits chained at its post. The ferry-house door stands open on nothing.

Inside, a rope hangs cut a yard off the floor, and the strongbox lies pried and empty on its side. Small clawed tracks cross the dust — not toward the water, but downriver, along the causeway, away from the crossing you meant to take.

Above, the loft boards creak once, then hold still, as if something up there is holding its breath to match yours.

payload.body: Arrived at Greyhollow Ford to find it abandoned. The ferry bell is gone and the ferry-keeper absent. The ferry sits chained at its post, the ferry-house door open. Inside: the bell-rope cut a yard from the floor, the strongbox pried open and emptied. Small clawed tracks lead downriver along the causeway, away from the crossing. Something moves in the loft above, holding still.
payload.title: The silent crossing at Greyhollow Ford

payload.body: The clawed tracks and cut rope suggest a non-human intruder, possibly small. The strongbox theft and bell removal appear deliberate. Something waits in the loft—uncertain if hostile or merely startled. The ferry-keeper's fate unknown.
payload.title: DM: Unknown threat at Greyhollow

payload.text: I search the ferry-house for whoever cut the bell rope.

payload.text: Easy now. Whatever's up there heard us before we heard it — best we don't greet it with steel first.
I call up to the loft, gently, offering no threat — asking whoever's hiding to come down and talk.

payload.body: Tamsin Vale searched the ferry-house for signs of who cut the bell rope, but found no evidence of the culprit. The ferry sits idle, its bell silenced, while full dark approaches across the ford.
payload.title: The Silent Bell at Greyhollow Ford
